title: Canonical scalar forgetting and inverse-image comparison
statement: For every commutative ring Λ of universe u+1 and schemes X,Y of universe u, construct the exact scalar-forgetting functor on constant-module sheaves, its canonical natural isomorphism f^*Mod ⋙ forget ≅ forget ⋙ f^*Ab for any f:X→Y, and the free represented generator map Z[U]→forget(Λ[U]). The inverse-image isomorphism is the composite of the Kan-extension and sheafification comparisons, not an arbitrarily chosen witness.

source.place: Tags 03D3 and 03D7; canonical construction also used in exists_upperStar_forget₂_natIso

proof.text: Use the canonical coefficientwise moduleAbelianForget, whose additivity and finite-limit preservation are proved in ModuleAbelianCoefficientComparison. Its finite-colimit preservation is constantModuleSheaves_forget_preservesColimits. The old forget name is a definitional abbreviation of this same functor, and its instances forward to the existing proofs.

Use the upstream pullbackIso, the inverse of moduleAbelianUpperStarIso, whose inverse component pullback is the abelian adjunction mate of the forgotten module unit. In Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.RawModuleScalarDerivedPullbackIso, pullback_unit proves that unit equation directly: by definition the comparison is the inverse image of the forgotten module unit under the abelian adjunction Hom equivalence, so Equiv.apply_symm_apply recovers that unit. No import of RawModuleScalarSheafComposition is needed. The theorem eq_pullback_of_unit proves uniqueness. The fully proved kanSheafification_eq_pullback identifies this particular map with the sheafified inverse Kan-extension comparison followed by sheafComposeNatTrans. Its proof expands both inverse-image units, applies sheafification-unit naturality and sheafComposeNatTrans_fac, and then leftKanExtensionCompIsoOfPreserves_inv_fac. Injectivity of the abelian adjunction Hom equivalence identifies the two maps. Thus the original canonical formula is retained as a library theorem, rather than only as a scratch regression. All formulas hold without nonempty, nonzero or finiteness hypotheses.

Retain the upstream freeAbelian and freeMap. They are the original constructions, definitionally unchanged after identifying forget with moduleAbelianForget: transpose the represented module identity section through abelian sheafification, the free-group adjunction, and Yoneda. All parent nodes continue to use these same canonical maps.

lean.statement:
abbrev pullbackIso (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f ⋙ moduleAbelianForget Λ X ≅
      moduleAbelianForget Λ Y ⋙ upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} f
lean.note: The canonical construction attachment remains upstream. Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.RawModuleScalarPullbackComparison is withdrawn after migrating both current direct consumers, OrdinaryFiniteP1Kummer and CartierRelativeBoundaryRealization, to Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.RawModuleScalarDerivedPullbackIso. The latter already reexports the upstream canonical constructions and retains forget, forget_additive, forget_preservesFiniteLimits and forget_preservesFiniteColimits as the same aliases and instances. It now also contains the three fully proved characterization theorems AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.RawModuleScalarComparison.pullback_unit, AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.RawModuleScalarComparison.eq_pullback_of_unit and AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.RawModuleScalarComparison.kanSheafification_eq_pullback, transferred verbatim from the withdrawn module. In particular the identification with the original Kan-extension/sheafification composite remains a library theorem. No construction, mathematical dependency, declaration signature or unit step is withdrawn. A current scan of lean/ and quarantine/ finds no other imports of the withdrawn Sheaf path.
